name: Private credit stress
value: Fitch: defaults elevated; BDC exits slowing
summary: Fitch says US private credit defaults remain elevated and nontraded BDC selling has slowed but stays significant
state: Fitch says the US private credit default rate remained elevated in the third quarter of 2026 (Newsquawk), and that the pace of investors selling nontraded BDC shares has slowed but remains significant, with redemption requests above the usual 5% quarterly cap (InvestmentNews). Searches on 20 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, no forced asset sales and no losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Investors in private credit and nontraded BDC funds may face limits on withdrawals. Companies that borrow from these funds face higher refinancing risk.
rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions and elevated defaults = Watch; no multi-fund gating or contagion (Alert)

sources.title: Newsquawk — Fitch says US private credit default rate remains elevated in Q3 2026
InvestmentNews — Pace of investors selling nontraded BDCs slows but remains significant, says Fitch

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
